text: Ritter died in 1810, while Oersted not only lived to see the event take place but brought it about himself. In 1803, Oersted returned to Copenhagen and applied for the university's chair in physics, but he was turned down, probably because he was regarded more as a philosopher than as a physicist. Nevertheless, he continued to experiment and lecture, publishing his results in German and Danish periodicals. In 1806, he achieved his ambition and became professor of physics at the University of Copenhagen, although he did not attain full professorship (ordinarius) until 1817.
